notes: Harness BGG lookup failed (401) and corpus index missing, so I searched live myself and opened real pages (BGG lookup for Turing Machine/Mastermind blocked at 403, so used Meeple Mountain review + Wikipedia as the openable sources). None collide at mechanism level: Mastermind gives per-peg (position+color) feedback from a manual human codemaker, static code, no mechanical device. Turing Machine gives binary pass/fail per independent verifier criterion via punch-card cutouts, no asymmetric role (all players solve the same fixed code), code never changes. Black Box gives per-probe hit/reflection/detour feedback about spatial atom positions, asymmetric hider/seeker but hidden state is static all game. Re-Pin's signal is a single continuous ordinal readout (how many chambers correct IN ORDER, gated by a staircase cam so it can't skip ahead) from ONE physical device per turn, with an asymmetric Locksmith role that rotates seats and may secretly re-pin exactly one chamber after a fail, decaying prior knowledge. That combination (ordinal-not-per-slot feedback + mid-game secret re-pinning + rotating asymmetric role) isn't present in any of the three. Turing Machine is the nearest by 'mechanical device replaces a human referee' framing, hence 'near' not 'far'.
